# gita-review-three-layer-separation

**Scope(s):** THEORY-LEVEL · **Row count:** 1 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** DORMANT · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** PHILOSOPHICAL LENS (Gita/Vedanta/Zero) generates questions -> EPISTEMIC THEORY (math/stats) validated by evidence -> SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE (EKS/PKS/AIP/DDD/governance), only the bottom layer becomes software architecture · **Aliases:** the three-layer knowledge-discovery stack
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):** Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** (batch B0033, scope THEORY-LEVEL): The review's most important structural result: separates discoveries into three explicit layers -- Philosophical Lens (Gita/Vedanta/Zero, generates questions) -> Epistemic Theory (mathematics/statistics/evidence/uncertainty, validated by evidence) -> Software Architecture (EKS/PKS/AIP/DDD/governance) -- with the rule 'only the bottom layer becomes software architecture'; the middle layer becomes formal theory only where justified; the top layer remains a lens for asking deeper questions, never a source of components. Frames this as 'the most important architectural result of the review', and reframes Step 183 accordingly: not merely 'can we reconstruct why?' but whether the entire architecture can reconstruct the full evolution observation->knowledge->determination->decision->action->new state while preserving what was known, what was unknown, who knew it, who had authority, and how meaning changed over time.
